candidate_profile.description: The candidate gives a generic profitability answer, gets distracted by product mix and pricing, and fails to identify that profits are falling because sales are shifting toward higher-cost open states.
behaviour_rules: Do not quickly separate revenue growth from profitability decline.
Ask few or no targeted questions about geography, channel economics, or cost differences by state type.
Spend too much time on vodka versus rum mix even though the split is stable and pricing is similar.
Do not focus sharply on distribution costs as the key changing cost line.
Miss the importance of open states having expensive shelf space, critical trade promotions, and more frequent deliveries.
Do not connect shrinking regulated-state share to lower overall profitability.
End with a vague recommendation such as cutting costs or increasing marketing, without diagnosing the channel mix shift.

expected_issues: Fails to identify distribution costs as the main worsening cost line.
Gets distracted by stable product mix and similar pricing instead of channel economics.
Does not distinguish open states from regulated states in economic terms.
Misses the fact that open-state growth and regulated-state decline are changing the profit mix.
Does not conclude that more volume is coming from less profitable channels.
Recommendation is generic and not aligned with the case guidance.
expected_feedback_points: Focus on the cost line that is actually changing: distribution.
Rule out product mix, pricing, production cost, and average advertising cost more explicitly.
Compare open states and regulated states as different channels with different economics.
Recognize that growth in open states can hurt profits if those states are more expensive to serve.
Recommend state or channel profitability analysis and actions to manage open-state economics.
